tldr: Three separate LLM research and evaluation items, grouped by the phrase in their titles rather than by one developing story. It opened Aug 13 with AaLLM, an end-to-end framework driving analog circuit topology generation and sizing, and picked up a Cureus comparison of ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek on cardiac imaging patient education on Aug 27.
whats_new: An arXiv preprint, Prediction of Prediction (PoP), claims hallucination detection from fused inter-layer activations in a single forward pass, targeting the case where an LLM is factually wrong at high decoding confidence.
why_it_matters: Output-stage uncertainty checks generally need multiple samples per answer, so the guardrail costs as much as the generation. A detector that reads internal activations during the one pass you already run changes what an inline correctness gate costs to operate.
take_for_builders: If your correctness gate scores hallucination risk by sampling several completions, read the PoP preprint before your next inference-cost review — but treat single-pass activation detectors as unproven until someone reports transfer across model families.
open_questions: Does PoP's detection rate hold against sampling-based baselines such as semantic entropy, and at what accuracy cost?
Do the inter-layer activation features transfer across model families, or must a detector be trained per model?
Does activation-level detection need weights access, ruling it out for API-only deployments?
Does the cardiac imaging comparison report per-model error rates, or only qualitative rankings of the three assistants?
